questions.question: Which of the following statement(s) are true with respect to the ethnic composition of Belgium? I. 59 percent of the total population of Belgium lives in the Wallonia region and speaks French. II. 40 percent live in the Flemish region and speak Dutch. III. One percent of the Belgians speak German. IV. In the capital city Brussels, 80 percent people speak French while 20 per cent are Dutch speaking.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II swap the figures; III and IV are correct (CBSE marking scheme: B).
option_feedback: Both are wrong: 59% live in the Flemish region and speak Dutch; 40% live in Wallonia and speak French.
I and II swap the regions and languages.

questions.question: Consider the following statements on Power Sharing and choose the correct statement(s): I. Imposing the will of the majority community over others. II. It helps in reducing the possibility of conflict between the social groups. III. Power Sharing is a good way to ensure the stability of political order. IV. questions.question:
Read the given text and answer the questions.

*"Sri Lanka emerged as an independent country in 1948. The leaders of the Sinhala community sought to secure dominance over government by virtue of their majority. As a result, the democratically elected government adopted a series of MAJORITARIAN measures to establish Sinhala supremacy. Over the years, it created feelings of alienation among the Sri Lankan Tamils... On the other hand, the Belgian leaders took a different path. They recognised the existence of regional differences and cultural diversities. Between 1970 and 1993, they amended their constitution four times to work out an arrangement that would enable everyone to live together within the same country."* (Adapted from Power Sharing, NCERT)

(i) State any one demand of the Tamils in Sri Lanka. (1)

(ii) State the result of the majoritarian government in Sri Lanka. (1)

(iii) Explain any two provisions of the Belgian model of power sharing. (2)
answer_steps: (i) Any one: recognition of Tamil as an official language; regional autonomy; equality of opportunity in securing education and jobs.
(ii) It created distrust between the Tamil and Sinhala communities, which turned into a civil war; thousands were killed and many families became refugees.

(iii) Any two: equal numbers of Dutch and French-speaking ministers in the central government; many powers given to state governments, which are not subordinate to the centre; a separate Brussels government with equal representation; community governments for cultural, educational and language issues.

questions.question: What are the different forms of power sharing in modern democracies? Give an example of each of these.
answer_steps: Horizontal: among the legislature, executive and judiciary (e.g. judges can check laws made by legislatures); vertical: among levels of government (e.g. union, state and local governments in India).
Among social groups: e.g. community government in Belgium, reserved constituencies in India.
Among political parties, pressure groups and movements: e.g. coalition governments; farmers' and traders' groups influencing decisions.

questions.question: State one prudential reason and one moral reason for power sharing with an example from the Indian context.
answer_steps: Prudential reason: power sharing reduces conflict between social groups and ensures political stability.
Example: reserved constituencies for Scheduled Castes and Tribes give them a share in power and reduce social tension.
Moral reason: power sharing is the spirit of democracy; people have a right to be consulted, as in panchayati raj where people govern their own villages.

questions.question: After reading this chapter, three students drew different conclusions. Thomman: power sharing is necessary only in societies which have religious, linguistic or ethnic divisions. Mathayi: power sharing is suitable only for big countries that have regional divisions. Ouseph: every society needs some form of power sharing even if it is small or does not have social divisions. Which of these do you agree with and why?
answer_steps: I agree with Ouseph.
Power sharing is the very spirit of democracy: people affected by decisions have a right to be consulted, whatever the size or diversity of the society.
Power sharing also prevents the concentration of power and the tyranny of the majority, so even small or uniform societies need it.

questions.question: The Mayor of Merchtem, a town near Brussels in Belgium, has defended a ban on speaking French in the town's schools. He said that the ban would help all non-Dutch speakers integrate in this Flemish town. Do you think that this measure is in keeping with the spirit of Belgium's power sharing arrangements? Give your reasons.
answer_steps: No, the measure is against the spirit of Belgium's power sharing arrangements.
Belgium's model is based on respecting all linguistic communities, with equal representation and community governments for language and education.
Banning French imposes one community's language on others, which could revive the tensions that Belgium's accommodation was designed to remove.

questions.question: Read the passage and pick out any one of the prudential reasons for power sharing offered in it: 'We want to give more power to the panchayats to realise the dream of Mahatma Gandhi... Giving power to panchayats is also a way to reduce corruption and increase administrative efficiency. When people participate in the planning and implementation of developmental schemes, they would naturally exercise greater control over these schemes. This would eliminate the corrupt middlemen...'
answer_steps: Prudential reason: giving power to panchayats reduces corruption and increases administrative efficiency.
When people plan and implement schemes, they control them and eliminate corrupt middlemen.

questions.question: Arguments in favour of power sharing are: A. reduces conflict among different communities; B. decreases the possibility of arbitrariness; C. delays decision making process; D. accommodates diversities; E. increases instability and divisiveness; F. promotes people's participation in government; G. undermines the unity of a country. Select the answer:
questions.explanation: Power sharing reduces conflict, checks arbitrariness, accommodates diversity and promotes participation.
option_feedback: C and G are arguments against.
C and E are arguments against power sharing.

questions.question: Consider: A. In Belgium, the Dutch-speaking majority people tried to impose their domination on the minority French-speaking community. B. In Sri Lanka, the policies of the government sought to ensure the dominance of the Sinhala-speaking majority. C. The transformation of Belgium from unitary government to a federal one prevented a possible division of the country on linguistic lines. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Belgium's leaders accommodated both communities instead of imposing majority rule.
option_feedback: A is wrong: in Belgium the French-speaking minority was richer; the Dutch did not impose domination.

questions.question: Match: (1) power shared among different organs of government, (2) among governments at different levels, (3) by different social groups, (4) by two or more political parties, with (A) community government, (B) separation of powers, (C) coalition government, (D) federal government. questions.question: Describe the majoritarian measures adopted in Sri Lanka.
answer_steps: In 1956, an Act recognised Sinhala as the only official language, disregarding Tamil.
Governments followed preferential policies that favoured Sinhala applicants for university positions and government jobs.
A new constitution stipulated that the state shall protect and foster Buddhism.

questions.question: How did majoritarianism affect Sri Lanka?
answer_steps: The Sri Lankan Tamils felt alienated and that their language, culture and equal rights were ignored.
Their demands for Tamil as an official language, regional autonomy and equal opportunities were denied; by the 1980s they demanded Tamil Eelam.
Distrust turned into a civil war: thousands were killed, many became refugees and lost livelihoods; the war ended only in 2009.

questions.question: Explain horizontal and vertical distribution of power with examples.
answer_steps: Horizontal distribution: power is shared among the legislature, executive and judiciary at the same level, creating checks and balances.
Example: in India, ministers are responsible to Parliament, and judges can check the executive and laws made by legislatures.
Vertical division: power is shared among governments at different levels, such as union, state and local (panchayat, municipality) governments.

questions.question: Explain the measures adopted by Belgium to accommodate its diversity.
answer_steps: Belgium amended its constitution four times between 1970 and 1993 to let everyone live together.
The number of Dutch and French-speaking ministers in the central government is equal, and some special laws need a majority from each linguistic group.
Many powers of the central government were given to state governments of the two regions, which are not subordinate to the centre.
Brussels has a separate government in which both communities have equal representation.

A third kind of government, the community government, elected by each language community, handles cultural, educational and language issues; this avoided civic strife, and Brussels became the EU headquarters.

questions.question: Describe the four forms of power sharing in modern democracies.
answer_steps: Horizontal distribution: among the legislature, executive and judiciary, with checks and balances (judges can check the executive and legislatures).
Vertical division: among governments at different levels, such as union and state (federal government), and local governments like panchayats and municipalities.
Among social groups: community government in Belgium; reserved constituencies for weaker sections and women in India.
Among political parties: competition ensures power does not stay in one hand; coalition governments share power directly.
Among pressure groups and movements: traders, businessmen, farmers and industrial workers influence decisions or join government committees.

questions.question:
Read the source and answer the questions.

*"Power sharing is good because it helps to reduce the possibility of conflict between social groups. Since social conflict often leads to violence and political instability, power sharing is a good way to ensure the stability of political order. Imposing the will of majority community over others may look like an attractive option in the short run, but in the long run it undermines the unity of the nation."* (NCERT)

(i) What kind of reason for power sharing is given here? (1)

(ii) What does imposing the will of the majority do in the long run? (1)

(iii) Give one moral reason for power sharing and explain it. (2)
answer_steps: (i) A prudential reason.
(ii) It undermines the unity of the nation.

(iii) Power sharing is the very spirit of democracy: people affected by decisions have a right to be consulted on how they are governed, and a legitimate government is one where citizens participate and acquire a stake in the system.

In the capital city Brussels, 80 per cent people speak French while 20 per cent are Dutch-speaking."* (NCERT)
